subject: math
title: Grade 1 Ways to Make 10
seo_title: Grade 1 Ways to Make 10 Worksheets: Free Math Practice with Answer Key (BC Curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Grade 1 math worksheets on ways to make 10 for the BC curriculum: ten frames, number bonds, pairs that make 10, missing parts like 7 + □ = 10 and simple word problems. 100 questions with pictures and an answer key.
key_big: Two numbers make 10 when they fill a ten frame: 7 and 3, 6 and 4, 5 and 5.
key_sub: Count the empty boxes to find how many more make 10. 6 + 5 is 11, not 10: the partner of 6 is 4.
body_html:
What does “make 10” mean?

Two numbers make 10 when they add up to 10.

A ten frame has 10 boxes. The full boxes are one part. The empty boxes are the other part.

Example

How many more make 10? The ten frame has 6 counters.

Count the empty boxes: 4. 6 + 4 = 10.

Answer: 4

Number bonds to 10

A number bond shows a whole and two parts. The whole is 10.

Pairs that make 10Turned around
1 + 99 + 1
2 + 88 + 2
3 + 77 + 3
4 + 66 + 4
5 + 55 + 5

Find the missing part

Think: what goes with this number to make 10?

Example

7 + □ = 10

Start at 7. Count on to 10: 8, 9, 10. That is 3.

Answer: 3

Example

Liam has 4 pucks. He wants 10. How many more?

4 + □ = 10. 4 + 6 = 10.

Answer: 6 more

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
7 counters: “7 more make 10”Count the empty boxes, not the full ones. 3 more make 10
6 + 5 = 106 + 5 = 11. The partner of 6 is 4: 6 + 4 = 10
7 + □ = 10, so □ = 17Do not add 10. Find the part: 7 + 3 = 10
Counting 7, 8, 9, 10 to get 4Do not count the 7. Say 8, 9, 10. That is 3

faq.q: What are ways to make 10 in Grade 1 math in BC?
faq.a: In the Number area of the BC Grade 1 math curriculum, students learn the ways to make 10, such as 7 and 3 or 6 and 4. They show them with ten frames, number bonds and objects.

faq.q: What are the pairs that make 10?
faq.a: 1 + 9, 2 + 8, 3 + 7, 4 + 6 and 5 + 5, plus the same pairs turned around, such as 9 + 1. 10 + 0 makes 10 too.

faq.q: Why do Grade 1 students use ten frames?
faq.a: A ten frame shows 10 boxes. Children can see how many are full and how many are empty, so they see both parts of 10 at once.

faq.q: How can I help my child practise ways to make 10 at home?
faq.a: Use 10 small objects, like buttons or blocks. Hide some under a cup and ask how many are hidden. A few minutes a day builds quick recall.
